messages:
irene: :rotating_light: paging oncall — alert from streaming-decode pool: repeated CUDA OOMs and container crashes on node gpu-rt-23. Spike started ~11:12 UTC

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: PD-2381. Severity: sev2. Assigned to irene

sam: seeing a flood of FAILED_PRECONDITION and status 13s in the router. Clients timing out. Any quick theory?

irene: initial traces point to runaway generation — some streams never terminate and the KV cache grows unbounded. Need to know if this is client misconfig or runtime bug.

matt: logs from gpu-rt-23 show repeated cudaMalloc OOM, then the decode container gets killed: 
```
[2026-03-15T11:12:34Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T11:12:34Z] node: pid=31241 service=decode-stream exit=137
[2026-03-15T11:12:35Z] watchdog: killed container decode-streamer on gpu-rt-23
```

olivia: digging into traces — one tenant (acme-retail) had client max_tokens set to 100000 and was streaming in a loop. Sequence length keeps growing past 4k, then 8k, then OOM.

sam: could be an SDK change on their side, or a malformed prompt. But we should fail fast for obviously bad params.

irene: @eng-runtime-lead can we push a guard at the gateway to clamp effective_max_tokens for streaming? Also need an emergency eviction for stalled streams.

eng-runtime-lead: rolling a hotpatch to prod-edge now: clamp streaming effective_max_tokens = min(max_tokens, 2048). Deploying to all edge pools.

oncall-bot: deploy start: edge-hotpatch/token-cap-v1 by eng-runtime-lead (sha abc123) — rolling to 8 regions

matt: lowered per-GPU concurrency on gpu-rt-23 to reduce simultaneous OOM cascade. Shrunk decode-pool replicas from 6 to 2 on that node.

olivia: added temporary routing rule to move new streaming traffic off gpu-rt-23. Applied `kubectl patch` to avoid restart loop.

sam: router queue is filling; can we set a short stream_queue_timeout so runaway connections fail fast?

eng-runtime-lead: set stream_queue_timeout=5s and short-circuit 400 for client max_tokens > 10000 at the router layer while we stabilize.

irene: ops note: approx 22% streaming failures over last 20m, concentrated in us-west. ACME had ~80 streams that never completed.

olivia: opened a ticket with ACME and looped in AE. Message: "We detected extreme max_tokens values causing backend OOMs; we've applied an emergency token cap and evicted stalled streams. Please review client config."

matt: restart of decode-service on gpu-rt-23 recovers the process but memory climbs quickly again — looks like KV cache not being freed for expired/stalled sessions.

sam: can runtime force-drop sessions with no progress for >60s and free their KV cache? That would stop the leak.

eng-runtime-lead: implemented evict_long_streams(age>60s) on the decode service and published an eviction metric. Triggered immediately.

oncall-bot: action log: evict_long_streams triggered 98 sessions in last 2m

irene: after eviction + gateway clamp, OOMs fell to near-zero on gpu-rt-23. Error rate trending down.

oncall-bot: deploy success: edge-hotpatch/token-cap-v1 completed in 00:01:40

matt: next steps — we need per-session memory accounting in runtime so a single bad client can't exhaust GPU memory. Also add a permanent hard cap and better telemetry for anomalous token params.

eng-runtime-lead: agreed. Will schedule per-session memory accounting and make the gateway cap permanent. Adding P0 work item.

olivia: customer-impact summary for postmortem: 
- impact window: 11:12–11:30 UTC, us-west; ~25% streaming failures in window
- root cause: unbounded client max_tokens causing runaway generation & KV cache growth -> GPU OOMs
- mitigations: emergency gateway token cap, evict_long_streams, restart decode on affected nodes, traffic diversion
- affected tenants: ~12, largest ACME (80 impacted streams)

sam: were there partial outputs or persisted PII? We need to be clear for customers.

irene: no persisted data leaked; streams aborted in-flight. We'll include timeline and logs in customer bulletin.

matt: action items captured: 
1) runtime: per-session mem accounting + reject over-budget streams (owner: eng-runtime)
2) gateway: permanent token cap + anomaly telemetry (owner: eng-runtime)
3) SDK: client-side max_tokens validation and sane defaults (owner: SDK team)
4) ops: OOM escalation runbook + playbook edits (owner: oncall docs)

eng-runtime-lead: I'll own 1 & 2, putting P0 tickets into the backlog now.

olivia: drafting support message to affected customers and coordinating with AE.

sam: PR ready: sdk#412 add client-side max_tokens sanity check (0 < max_tokens <= 4096)

irene: handoff to next oncall at 12:00 UTC. Summary: misconfigured client params caused GPU OOMs; emergency mitigations applied and system stabilized; follow-ups assigned. See PD-2381 for full notes.

oncall-bot: PD-2381 status changed to monitoring. Acknowledged by irene

olivia: :thumbsup: attaching logs/metrics to the postmortem doc and closing thread for now.

matt: saved commands for archive: 
```
kubectl -n infra logs decode-streamer-72 -c runtime | grep -E "cudaMalloc|KVCache|evict"
```

sam: final: small SDK validation PR merged.

irene: thanks everyone — handoff complete.
